answers.ask: Which of the ten maps should be built first, and do they all reuse one runway layout or is each map its own?
answers.answer: Build Luxury Mall first as the core launch map. Each map should be its own themed environment, while using the same standard runway gameplay layout for a smaller, consistent first build.

answers.ask: How many players per server? Runway length and lobby capacity both depend on it.
answers.answer: Use 10 players per server, keeping the runway show manageable while everyone receives their 20-second turn. The lobby should comfortably hold those 10 players.

answers.ask: Are the apartments part of the same map or a separate instanced space?
answers.answer: Apartments should be separate instanced spaces so home decorating and friend visits do not interfere with active fashion-show rounds.

scene_prompt: Create the core 3D launch map for a multiplayer fashion runway game: a Luxury Mall themed environment for 10 players. Arrange a comfortable central lobby that holds all players, with a standard runway-show layout featuring a long catwalk, model entrance, audience/viewing area, and a top-three winners’ podium. Surround the show space with mall shopping and styling zones for clothing, body, hair, makeup, accessories, and shoes, plus a designer studio and photo studio. Luxury apartments are separate instanced home spaces, not part of the active mall map. Future maps are distinct themed environments but reuse this consistent runway layout.
agent_notes: The doc self-declares Dress-Up, Social Roleplay and Life Simulation, and the loop is style-an-outfit-then-walk-the-runway, so Roleplay & Avatar Sim leads on the Dress Up preset: stage-runway is the shape because the dress phase, the walk and the voting crowd are precisely a catwalk fed by preparation space with the audience around it. The lobby, timed rounds, map voting and star scoring are Party & Casual's territory, so it is named as secondary and contributes tracker-leaderboard for the fashion levels and magazine-cover wall; I did not take space-staged, since players watch each other's 20-second walks rather than being sealed out of the stage, so social-hub carries the lobby instead. Both modifiers come from the author's own answers rather than from my reading: apartments are enterable and decorated, which is P3, and they are explicitly separate instanced spaces while each of the ten themed maps is its own environment, which is P4 — worth flagging upstream since P4 and P3 are not shipping yet, and the answers also scope the first build to Luxury Mall with one reused runway layout. Two things I decided without a user: teleporter-link as the marked entry from the venue into the instanced apartments, which would otherwise be unreachable, and the top-three podium, which no loaded option covers so it sits on the runway stage as part of the results area rather than as its own pick.
